qs.q: Which routine laboratory study is included in the evaluation of pediatric ALL to assess for tumor lysis syndrome or metabolic derangements?
qs.e: Serum chemistries, uric acid levels, and LDH levels are routine laboratory studies in pediatric ALL, which help evaluate complications like tumor lysis syndrome. Thyroid or pancreatic tests are not part of this standard initial workup.

qs.q: Which condition is a classic cause of tumor lysis syndrome leading to acute kidney injury?
o: Obstruction of tubules by uric acid crystals
Thrombosis of the main renal artery
qs.e: Tumor lysis syndrome is a specific form of AKI primarily caused by the obstruction of renal tubules by uric acid crystals from cell lysis. Ureteropelvic junction obstruction is a congenital postrenal cause, not related to cell lysis.

qs.q: A patient receiving chemotherapy develops tumor lysis syndrome. Massive apoptosis of tumor cells would be expected to release all of the following EXCEPT:
qs.e: Apoptotic cells maintain membrane integrity and are phagocytosed without releasing contents or causing inflammation. IL-1 is a pro-inflammatory cytokine NOT released during apoptosis. K+, LDH, and phosphate are released during NECROSIS (which can follow massive apoptosis if clearance is overwhelmed), but the question asks about apoptosis itself.
